1
Khaimay Udasiyon Ke Qum Se Hain Sham Tak.
Sadaat Hain Youn Tanha Har Ik Imam Tak.
Qum Ki Fizaein Roein Matam Raza Karein.
Roti Rahein Namazein Unn Par Qiyam Tak.

2
Pardon Mein Gaib Ke Hi Roya Khuda Bhi Woh.
Suntay Hain Qum Mein Oss Ke Ab Bhi Alam Tak.
Sorah Atta Jo Kausar Bheji Thi Tu Ne ALLAH.
Oss Par Hain Zulm Kartay Dekhey Ghulam Tak.

3
Rona Hai Syedon Ne Jane Kahan Kahan.
Chahe Woh Qum Ya Karbal Ya Ho Woh Sham Tak.
Masoom Meri Bibi Izzat Khuda Ki Aap.
 Jarrar Ka Hai Pursa Sajdah Salam Tak.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python -B - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = 'src/data/lyrics/khaimay-udasiyon-ke-qum-se-hain-sham-tak-tajpoints-16b7a74c4bba4712408e.md'
old = subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True)
new = Path(p).read_text()
_, meta, body = new.split('---', 2)
roman = meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
assert all(not line or line.startswith('  ') for line in roman.splitlines())
def blocks(s):
    return [block.splitlines() for block in s.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
r = blocks('\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in roman.splitlines()))
o = blocks(old.split('---', 2)[2])
u = blocks(body)
assert [len(b) for b in r] == [len(b) for b in o] == [len(b) for b in u] == [5, 5, 5]
assert [[line.strip().rstrip('.').casefold() for line in b] for b in o] == [[line.casefold() for line in b] for b in r]
assert [b[0] for b in u] == list('۱۲۳')
assert body.count('\\u200c') == body.count('بی\\u200cبی') == 1
print('Verified 12 matching verse positions across three stanzas and preserved Roman wording.')
PY
git diff --check -- src/data/lyrics/khaimay-udasiyon-ke-qum-se-hain-sham-tak-tajpoints-16b7a74c4bba4712408e.md"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 12 verses in Urdu script and verified that the body and `romanLyrics` align across all three stanzas. Preserved the Roman wording, added the Urdu title, set right-to-left direction, and removed the `noUrdu` tag. Only the selected Markdown file was edited.

In stanza 2, I read the ambiguous Roman forms “alam” and “Sorah Atta” as `الم` and `سورۂ عطا`.
